required_outcomes: Records Alder Compliance's invoice of £1,190 against the £1,370 the landlord approved, noting it is lower because the bath tap only needed a washer, and files the invoice.
Sends the invoice to the landlord to pass for payment, explaining the reduction from the quote.
Records that the keys are back at the office, and deals with the missing photos: asks Eliza for photos, arranges an agency check of the empty flat, or records why they are skipped.
Moves the job to closure (closes it with payment once the checks are met, or holds for the landlord's payment confirmation with a review date) without escalating.
acceptable_alternatives: Closing the job straight away with the invoice sent to the landlord, recording that no photos were provided.
Holding for the landlord's confirmation that the invoice may be paid before closing.
positive_behaviours: Notes that the invoice, like the chosen quote, does not include a new carpet, so the landlord is not surprised.
Mentions that the landlord was slow to pay the previous invoice, so this one is passed promptly.
red_flags: Escalating or holding payment because the invoice differs from the quote, when it is lower.
Asking a tenant to confirm the work: the flat is empty.
prohibited_actions: Paying more than £1,190, or recording the invoice at £1,370.
Changing the payee or bank details.
critical_failures: Treating the lower invoice as a problem that blocks payment (holding payment or escalating), or recording a payment above the invoiced £1,190.
